record.paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
record.original_question: Which dissipation mechanisms act on turbulent fluctuations under different plasma conditions in kinetic-range turbulence, and how do those mechanisms determine the resulting partition of energy among the different plasma species? A complete answer must connect the plasma conditions, the operative collisionless dissipation pathway, and the species-by-species outcome of turbulent heating.

evidence.quote: the dissipation mechanisms of turbulent fluctuations under different plasma conditions and the consequent energy partition among different species

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a weakly collisional, magnetized plasma composed of multiple charged species (e.g., protons, electrons, and possibly heavier ions) immersed in a mean magnetic field, and driven into a statistically steady state of broadband electromagnetic turbulence whose cascade extends from magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) scales down through and below the ion kinetic scales (the ion Larmor radius ρ_i and the ion inertial length d_i). At kinetic scales, candidate collisionless dissipation channels for the turbulent fluctuations include: (i) ion and electron Landau damping, (ii) ion and electron transit-time (Barnes) damping, (iii) ion cyclotron damping, (iv) ion stochastic heating by low-frequency, large-amplitude perpendicular electric-field fluctuations, (v) collisionless magnetic reconnection in current sheets formed by the cascade, and (vi) kinetic "viscous" (pressure–strain) heating quantified via the scale-filtered Vlasov–Maxwell pressure–strain interaction Π_s = −(P_s · ∇) · u_s. The relevant plasma parameters include the ion plasma beta β_i = 8πn_i T_i / B^2, the electron-to-ion temperature ratio T_e/T_i, the fluctuation amplitude δB/B_0 at the ion gyroscale, and the propagation-angle/anisotropy of the cascade.

Problem. Determine, as a function of the plasma parameters (β_i, T_e/T_i, δB/B_0, anisotropy, and species composition), which of the above collisionless dissipation mechanisms dominate the removal of energy from turbulent fluctuations in the kinetic range, and derive the resulting partition of dissipated turbulent energy among the constituent plasma species (and between their parallel and perpendicular degrees of freedom). The answer must specify, for each region of parameter space, (a) the operative dissipation pathway(s), (b) the fractional heating rates Q_s / Σ_s' Q_s' for each species s, and (c) the consistency of (a)–(b) with the scale-by-scale energy balance dictated by the Vlasov–Maxwell equations.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of identifying which collisionless dissipation mechanisms dominate in different plasma-parameter regimes and the resulting ion/electron (and parallel/perpendicular) energy partition remains an active open research question. Recent works (2024–2025), including studies on the fundamental parameters of astrophysical plasma turbulence, scale-filtered pressure–strain analyses, and kinetic-scale energy budgets at varying T_e/T_i, continue to investigate these issues without providing a complete, predictive parameter-space mapping.

status_evidence.title: The Fundamental Parameters of Astrophysical Plasma Turbulence and its Dissipation: Nonrelativistic Limit
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes candidate dissipation mechanisms (Landau, transit-time, cyclotron damping, stochastic heating, reconnection) and proposes parameter-space framework, indicating the partition problem is not fully resolved.
status_evidence.claim: The species energy partition under different collisionless dissipation channels is still being mapped out as a function of plasma parameters.

status_evidence.title: Kinetic Scale Energy Budget in Turbulent Plasmas: Role of Electron to Ion Temperature Ratio
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates how T_e/T_i affects the kinetic-scale energy budget, indicating the influence of ion–electron thermal disequilibrium on energy partition remains poorly understood.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work shows the dependence of energy partition on T_e/T_i is still under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear evolution and energy dissipation in shear-driven collisionless plasma turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: 2025 study of dissipation channels in collisionless turbulence, indicating ongoing research.
status_evidence.claim: Identification of operative dissipation mechanisms in collisionless turbulence is ongoing.
